pr_title: Fix TextureAtlas sampling from wrong index
pr_body:
# Objective

Fixes #4162 

## Solution

To prevent incorrect sampling in TextureAtlas's we reduce the UV rect by half the size of a texel.
pr_comments:
I like this refactor a lot better! Can you resolve my comments now, so other reviewers can get a clear sense of what needs to be done still?

Next: do we have a way to write a test for this, to both verify the fix and avoid regressions?

@alice-i-cecile I'm not sure how to write a test for this so if you or @StarArawn have any suggestions that would be great.

I now also think maybe shrinking by half a texel is too extreme and might cause issues for other sampling methods. Instead shrinking by e-6 might be better? I'll read up on filtering methods when I have time to double check.

Hmm. I took a look, and I don't understand this section of the code base well enough to give you confident advice.

We could do a very scoped unit test, but it's not clear how we would make that robust or generalize it to other strategies.

Or, we couldn try to do a full integration test suite for this class of error, verifying that we're not getting weird results regardless of the size of the texture atlas or sampling method.

The latter is probably out of scope for this PR: AIUI we don't have a "golden image" setup in place, nor do we have a property-based testing framework setup for rendering.

The problem with this approach is that the interpolated UVs will be changed for all fragments within the sprite. I thought perhaps there would instead be a way to clamp the UVs to stay within the half pixel boundary around the edge of the sprite to not sample outside it. This clamping should be done inside the fragment shader itself. Nical on Discord said that this is what webrender does and if it is good enough for them, I’m sure it’s good enough for us.
Ping? This PR would need to be reworked to do the adjustment in the shader.

issue_context.title: TextureAtlas texture sampling can sample from the wrong atlas index
issue_context.body:
## Bevy version

0.6.1, also main

## Operating system & version

Windows 10

## What you did

- Created a tilemap with 16x16 px tiles using a TextureAtlas
- Map was of size ~25x25 tiles
- Ortho camera
- MSAA set to 1
- Filtering set to Nearest
- Panned the camera and changed the camera scaling while experimenting

## What you expected to happen

I expected the grid to render "correctly", i.e. no gaps between tiles, proper textures applied, etc.

## What actually happened

Under certain zooms and camera positions 1px wide "tears" occurred that would span a row or a column (image attached [0]). Those tears use texture data from an adjacent TextureAtlas index.

## Additional information

I believe the issue is with this line here https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/crates/bevy_sprite/src/render/mod.rs#L478 and I tested a fix which seems to work but I want to confirm it makes sense before I create a PR.

To explain the issue (as I understand it), imagine you have a texture atlas with two sub-textures placed horizontally. Computing the uv rectangle for the second "sub-texture" (index 1) results in the uv verts [(0.5, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0), (0.5, 1.0)]. The problem arises with 0.5 being right on the border of the two textures. Due to numerical inaccuracies with floats I believe we can end up sampling with a value like 0.49999 even though index 1 was specified, resulting in the wrong texel being selected in the shader.

Proposed fix: change the computed rectangle size of sub-textures by shrinking them by the extent of a texel on all sides. In the above example if each sub-texture is a 1x1 px image, the texel size would be (0.5, 1.0) - and the mid point of the first texel would be (0.25, 0.5) and the midpoint of the second texel would be (0.75, 0.5). So instead of starting from 0.5 for the sampling u value we should start from 0.75 and also end there as well since we would subtract 0.25 from the high u values as well. This would prevent any small numerical errors from causing a sampling from the wrong sub-texture.

In code, the proposed solution would change:
```rust
                        *uv = (rect.min + *uv * rect_size) / current_image_size;
```
to
```rust
                        *uv = (rect.min + *uv * rect_size
                            + *uv * Vec2::new(-1.0, -1.0)
                            + Vec2::new(0.5, 0.5)) / current_image_size;
```

I think this would work for Nearest filtering but I'm not sure of the implications it might have on other modes.

Apologies if the terms above were not used correctly, not really an expert in graphics :)

[0] Here's an image of the "tearing" 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1036570/157405828-d6c19985-a847-416f-b61d-b3a5b9650d86.png)

After some experimenting, the colors in the tear come directly from the texture line right above the first line of the current index being specified.
